name: C++
description: Systems programming in modern C++. I wrote Achilles, my rigid-body simulator, in C++20 from the SIMD layout to the contact solver, plus ARUW's odometry and path tracking and the OpenArm controllers.

name: Performance & SIMD
description: Making code fast by design: data layouts, vectorization and measuring where the time goes. Achilles steps eight robots per SIMD instruction and outruns MuJoCo single-threaded.

name: Python
description: My main language for robotics tooling and research code: the VLA evaluation harness, my additions to the lab's arm planner, the Quest teleop, and the analysis behind ARUW's localization study.

name: Kinematics & Dynamics
description: How robots move and why: forward and inverse kinematics, rigid-body dynamics and the math that steps them. Achilles's O(n) dynamics, its integrators and contact solver, and the OpenArm IK fix.

name: Motion planning
description: Finding motions that reach a goal without hitting anything, and timing them so the robot can follow. ArmGroup's joint two-arm planning, SKIDADDLE's physics-aware paths and the peg reset.

name: Control systems
description: Making a robot track what it's asked to do. I led ARUW's move from pure pursuit to LQR path tracking that models the chassis's accelerations.

name: Impedance control
description: Controlling how stiff or compliant a robot arm feels instead of just where it goes. I wrote three impedance controllers for the OpenArms before settling on the motors' own loop.

name: State estimation
description: Working out where a robot is from noisy sensors. Kalman-filter odometry for ARUW's engineer, an error model for the sentry's lidar-inertial localization, and merged lidar scans on OpenDubs.

name: ROS 2
description: The Robot Operating System, the middleware most of OpenDubs runs on. Lidar merging and SLAM, the arms' control stack, parallel arm execution and the team's Docker environment.

name: Simulation (MuJoCo)
description: Physics simulation to develop and check robot software before hardware. I benchmarked Achilles against MuJoCo and planned OpenDubs's arms in it.

name: Robot learning
description: Robots that learn their behavior from data: vision-language-action models and reinforcement learning. I built and ran the VLA benchmark for the ARCHITECT paper, and a reset for online RL.

name: Teleoperation
description: Driving a robot live through a human operator. I built Quest teleop for OpenDubs's arms and used it to run live demos.

name: Hardware bring-up
description: Getting new hardware working end to end: computers, drivers, sensors and the environment the team develops in. The Jetson Thor and drive base, and OpenDubs's two lidars.

name: Java
description: The language of FIRST Tech Challenge robots. SKIDADDLE, my path-following library, and Live View, which streams camera video as text.

name: Experiment design
description: Setting up measurements so the answer can be trusted. The Odin localization campaign against motion capture, its error model, and the VLA benchmark's fair-test design.

name: Technical leadership
description: Setting the direction for a team's technical work. As FTC captain I ran a two-robot build plan, and at ARUW I led the LQR path-tracking rewrite.

name: Open source
description: Publishing and contributing code others use. My fix to the lab's IK solver landed upstream, and SKIDADDLE is a public FTC library.

name: Public speaking
description: Presenting to audiences outside the lab. The Introduction to FIRST speech at the U.S. Embassy in Gaborone and talks to students there.

name: Teaching & outreach
description: Teaching robotics and bringing it to new people. FIRST LEGO League sessions with students in Botswana and a local FLL team.

name: CAD
description: Computer-aided design of mechanical parts.

name: Kalman filtering
description: Estimating a robot's state by blending a motion model with noisy measurements. I rewrote ARUW's engineer odometry as Kalman filters and tuned them from logged drives, and fed optical flow into ArduPilot's EKF on OpenDubs.

name: LQR
description: The linear-quadratic regulator: optimal feedback for a linear model, from the Riccati equation. ARUW's new path tracking uses it on a world-frame model of the chassis.

name: Path following
description: Keeping a moving robot on a planned path at speed. SKIDADDLE for FTC robots, and LQR path tracking for ARUW's chassis against pure pursuit.

name: Trajectory generation
description: Turning a path into speeds and accelerations the robot can deliver. SKIDADDLE's look-ahead and precomputed speed limits, the LQR tracker's speed profile, and ArmGroup's 125 Hz retiming.

name: Splines and Bézier curves
description: Smooth curves for robot paths. SKIDADDLE follows cubic Bézier and Hermite splines, and the LQR tracker fits a cubic spline reparametrized by arc length.

name: Holonomic drive
description: Robots with mecanum or omni wheels that move in any direction. SKIDADDLE plans in the four wheels' motor space, and OpenDubs's first base drove four mecanum wheels.

name: Sensor fusion
description: Combining several sensors into one better estimate. Dead wheels with an IMU on ARUW's engineer, optical flow with an IMU on OpenDubs, and two lidars merged into one scan.

name: Odometry
description: Tracking a robot's position from its own motion. Dead-wheel odometry for ARUW and optical-flow odometry for OpenDubs, both checked against ground truth.

name: SLAM
description: Simultaneous localization and mapping: building a map while locating the robot in it. slam_toolbox on OpenDubs's merged lidar scan, and the Odin's relocalization into a prebuilt map on ARUW's sentry.

name: Nav2
description: The ROS 2 navigation stack. I set it up on OpenDubs's merged lidar scan, where it drove the robot point to point in simulation.

name: Lidar
description: Laser range sensors for mapping and localization. Two RPLIDAR A1s merged on OpenDubs, the Odin1 lidar-inertial sensor and the LD19 2D lidar characterized for ARUW.

name: Motion capture
description: Camera systems that track objects to a fraction of a millimeter, used as ground truth. I checked OpenDubs's odometry and ARUW's Odin localization against it.

name: Statistical modeling
description: Describing measured behavior with a model that predicts it. The Odin's error model: a relocalization offset plus first-order Gauss-Markov noise, checked on held-out data.

name: Monte Carlo methods
description: Answering questions by simulating many random outcomes. I validated the Odin's error model by simulating it many times along a held-out session's real path.

name: Data analysis
description: Turning logs and measurements into answers. The Odin and LD19 characterization, tuning ARUW's odometry from logged drives, and scoring the VLA benchmark.

name: Benchmarking
description: Measuring systems against each other fairly. Achilles against MuJoCo, four VLAs on a real robot, SKIDADDLE against Road Runner and Pedro Pathing, and LQR against pure pursuit.

name: VLA benchmarking
description: Testing vision-language-action models on real robot tasks. My harness ran π0, π0.5, GR00T N1.7 and MolmoAct2 on a Franka for the ARCHITECT paper.

name: Vision-language-action models
description: Robot policies that map camera images and an instruction straight to actions. I benchmarked four of them and studied where they fail.

name: LLMs for robotics
description: Using large language models to program robots. The ARCHITECT paper compares LLM-written robot programs, fixed with a few words from a person, against VLAs.

name: Reinforcement learning
description: Learning behavior by trial and reward. Achilles was built to make RL training faster, and my automatic reset lets arms practise online RL without a person.

name: Rigid-body dynamics
description: How connected rigid bodies move under forces. Achilles computes it with the Articulated Body Algorithm and checks it against MuJoCo and exact equations of motion.

name: Lagrangian mechanics
description: Deriving equations of motion from energy. I used the double pendulum's exact Lagrangian equations as ground truth for Achilles's dynamics.

name: Numerical integration
description: Stepping a simulation forward in time without it drifting. Semi-implicit Euler, velocity Verlet and implicit midpoint in Achilles, compared on energy.

name: Linear algebra
description: Vectors, matrices and spatial algebra. Achilles's own SIMD spatial algebra, and ARUW's Kalman filters split from 8×8 matrices into 2×2 ones.

name: Collision detection
description: Finding which bodies touch. Achilles's broad and narrow phases on one sphere-swept-box shape, and arm-against-arm checks in ArmGroup's plans.

name: Contact dynamics
description: What happens when bodies touch: contact forces and friction. Achilles's soft-contact solver with a Coulomb friction cone.

name: Inverse kinematics
description: Finding joint angles that put a robot's hand where you want it. I fixed the lab's analytical IK solver for the OpenArm, which teleop and planning both use.

name: Gravity compensation
description: Cancelling a robot arm's own weight so it holds still or moves freely. OpenDubs's arms run 500 Hz gravity compensation from Pinocchio's RNEA.

name: Real-time control
description: Control loops that must run on time, every time. 500 Hz arm control on OpenDubs, motors started on one shared timestamp, and odometry on ARUW's robot controller.

name: Bimanual manipulation
description: Robots using two arms at once. Planning both OpenArms together, running them in parallel, and driving both on teleop.

name: Manipulation
description: Robot arms grasping and moving things. OpenDubs's arms, the Fleet RL peg reset, and the VLA benchmark's pick-and-place, drawer and cloth tasks.

name: Concurrency
description: Code that does several things at once safely. Each arm runs from its own thread against one start stamp, with the shared MuJoCo model behind a lock.

name: Data-oriented design
description: Organizing a program around how its data is laid out and accessed. Achilles stores every field as a structure of arrays, with passes that declare what they read and write.

name: Software architecture
description: Designing how a system's parts fit together. Achilles V2 and V3, SKIDADDLE's controllers, scheduler and allocator, and one harness for every VLA.

name: Testing and validation
description: Proving code is right before trusting it. Achilles's compile-time checks and CI death tests, its dynamics against MuJoCo and exact answers, and a staged hardware bring-up for the arms.

name: Performance profiling
description: Measuring where a program spends its time and memory. A Valgrind trace showed nearly 89% of Achilles's data accesses are whole 8-lane vector loads and stores.

name: Computer graphics
description: Drawing 3D scenes. Achilles's OpenGL viewer renders every body from the simulation's own state.

name: OpenGL
description: The graphics API behind Achilles's viewer: one cube on the GPU, scaled and placed per body.

name: Computer vision
description: Getting information from camera images. Camera calibration for the peg reset, whose AprilTag tagging I designed with a teammate, and Live View's image processing.

name: Camera calibration
description: Measuring a camera's lens and where it sits. I calibrated the Fleet RL cameras with a ChArUco board and fit their poses to the arm.

name: Image processing
description: Transforming images pixel by pixel. Live View converts frames to the Lab colour space and dithers them into Braille characters.

name: Networking
description: Moving data between machines. The VLA harness talks WebSockets, ZMQ and HTTP, and the Quest teleop page streams poses over a websocket.

name: Web development
description: Building for the browser. The Quest teleop is a WebXR page the headset opens in AR, streaming the controllers to the robot.

name: JavaScript
description: The language of the Quest teleop page, which streams controller poses to the robot.

name: Embedded systems
description: Software on small computers inside robots. An optical-flow sensor over micro-ROS on an M5Stack, and odometry on ARUW's robot controller.

name: ArduPilot
description: Open-source autopilot firmware. OpenDubs's first base drove through a Pixhawk running ArduPilot, whose EKF I fed with optical flow.

name: Gazebo
description: A robot simulator for ROS. I gave OpenDubs a URDF and SDF for it and replayed the lidar mapping in it.

name: MuJoCo
description: A fast physics engine for robotics. Achilles's reference and benchmark, and where OpenDubs's arms are planned, simulated and tested.

name: Pinocchio
description: A rigid-body dynamics library. My OpenArm controllers and the 500 Hz gravity compensation use it.

name: Docker
description: Containers for reproducible environments. I set up the Docker environment the OpenDubs team develops in on the Jetson Thor.

name: Linux
description: The operating system under all of it. Flashing JetPack on the Jetson Thor and udev rules that name OpenDubs's two identical lidars.

name: NVIDIA Jetson
description: NVIDIA's embedded computers. OpenDubs runs on a Jetson Thor that I flashed and set up for the team.

name: CAN bus
description: The bus most robot motors talk on. OpenDubs's Thor sends the arms' motor targets over CAN-FD.

name: Debugging
description: Tracking a failure to its cause. A singularity in the lab's IK solver, a missing sensor mounting that sent odometry 155 m off, and identical lidars on USB.

name: Robot safety
description: Keeping robots and people safe. Arm goals checked against joint and torque limits, arms that cancel together, and a watchdog with speed caps on the Odin test platform.

name: Research
description: Asking a question and answering it rigorously. Co-authoring the ARCHITECT paper's VLA benchmark, and the Odin characterization that decided the sentry's localization.

name: Technical writing
description: Explaining technical work clearly. I wrote the ARCHITECT paper's VLA failure analysis, and design documents like Achilles V3's.

name: Project planning
description: Planning how work gets done. The FTC two-robot build plan, the LQR proposal, and the Odin test campaign's protocol.

name: Mentoring
description: Helping others learn. Teaching programming to a local FLL team and to students in Gaborone.

name: Advocacy
description: Making the case to decision makers. At the U.S. Embassy in Gaborone we advocated for STEM funding and lower tariffs on educational STEM goods.

name: Live demos
description: Showing a robot working in front of people. OpenDubs for Winbond, Fauna Robotics and ARCS donors, and robot demos at the U.S. Embassy event.

name: Collaboration
description: Building things with a team. The OpenDubs undergrad team, ARUW's competition robots, the Fleet RL tagging work and the HCRL benchmark.

name: Competitive robotics
description: Building robots to win competitions. ARUW in DJI's ARC and my FTC team's robots, path following and driver tools.
